transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-23
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Alicia Gomez (Wyvern), Ben Carter (Wyvern), Sofia Li (Wyvern), Tom Reed (Wyvern)

Summary:
Wyvern is planning to extend their existing contract by one year and add dedicated capacity in EU and APAC. Main blockers are: finalizing pricing for APAC region, security/KMS requirements for PHI-adjacent workloads, and an onsite network checklist for VPC peering. Redwood to provide updated quote, perf benchmarks, and private deployment checklist. Pilot kickoff proposed early February.

Topics:
- Contract extension logistics and term length
- APAC and EU capacity provisioning timeline
- Private deployment vs Dedicated reserved capacity trade-offs
- Security/compliance: SOC2, encryption/KMS, audit logs
- Benchmark plan for throughput/latency

Action items (short):
- Draft addendum & pricing (Redwood)
- Perf benchmark template (Redwood SE)
- Compliance doc list (Wyvern security)
- VPC peering details (Wyvern infra)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everybody, thanks for joining — uh — appreciate you carving time. Quick roll call, we'll just cover extension ask, region ramp, and then jump into security items.
[00:12] Alicia Gomez: Yep thanks Maya, Alicia here. We allocated an hour but we can move quick.
[00:16] Ben Carter: Ben — infra. Sofia and Tom as well.
[00:20] Tom Reed: Tom, hi.
[00:23] Ravi Patel: Ravi from Redwood, I'm the solutions engineer on the account.
[00:27] Lena Ortiz: Lena, CSM. Hi all.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Great. Quick context: Wyvern's been on Redwood Hosted for 9 months, you have a small Dedicated pool in US-east and usage has climbed 3x q/q. You're asking to extend the contract and add dedicated pools in EU-west and APAC regions, plus tie into your KMS for key wrapping. Is that all correct?
[00:46] Alicia Gomez: That's right. We did the initial burst in US-east early last year, traffic ramped faster than expected once the new triage feature rolled out. We need predictable throughput for our clinical summarization pipelines — and we have some data residency constraints in EU. APAC is mainly for latency to our partners in Singapore and Tokyo.
[01:06] Maya Chen: Cool. On the extension, you're looking at a 12-month extension and an increase to the committed GPUs by about 40% overall?
[01:13] Alicia Gomez: Yeah roughly 40% — we ran a quick projection and that gets us through Q4 next year.
[01:18] Ben Carter: One nuance — some of the APAC traffic is bursty, so we need to understand burst capacity and how fast Redwood can scale without cold starts. Also ECR, I mean — sorry — VPC network stuff.
[01:30] Ravi Patel: No worries. Burst capacity is available as a configurable option on Dedicated. We can do reserved baseline + burst buckets. For cold start minimization we keep warm kernels and ongoing KV caching, so tail latency stays low. FWIW some of the model variants we recommend for cost in APAC are the quantized ones — small memory footprint.
[01:46] Sofia Li: Can you spell KV cache? I've seen it referenced as K-V in our docs but sometimes it's different.
[01:50] Ravi Patel: K-V cache, key-value cache for attention state — apologies for the jargon.
[01:53] Sofia Li: Okay great, thanks.
[01:55] Tom Reed: On the SOC2/PHI angle: our legal team flagged that while we don't store actual PHI in Redwood, some of the outputs are derivative. We need assurance around encryption at rest and in transit, audit logs retention for 1 year, and an HSM-backed KMS. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys and HSM?
[02:14] Maya Chen: Yes — Private deployments support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations. For Hosted we support BYOK via KMS integrations in Dedicated tiers as well, but we need to validate the exact HSM provider. We'll share the KMS integration notes.
[02:28] Sofia Li: We also need to confirm where logs live — like request metadata, prompts, and token usage — that needs to be auditable and retained.
[02:36] Lena Ortiz: We can surface token-level logs in the Console with retention settings; for Private you control the storage, for Dedicated we can enable audit export to your S3 with lifecycle rules.
[02:46] Ben Carter: Good — on networking, we can't have open egress; VPC peering, CIDR ranges, and mutual TLS or private link would be preferred. What's the recommended approach?
[02:56] Ravi Patel: For Dedicated we support VPC peering and AWS PrivateLink. For Private on-prem we have VPN or direct connect options. We'll send the network checklist — it includes CIDR size, endpoint IP ranges, ports and TLS cert fingerprints.
[03:10] Alicia Gomez: Cool. On pricing: APAC pricing looks higher in the draft we saw. Can you explain what drives that?
[03:18] Maya Chen: Sure — APAC incurs higher infra costs and sometimes smaller instance availability. There are also replication and multi-AZ factors for redundancy. We price APAC as a region uplift and include optional reserved capacity discounts if you commit for 12 months.
[03:31] Tom Reed: Is there a way to do a hybrid — Dedicated in US + Private in EU, and Hosted in APAC as a stopgap? We're trying to minimize network complexity while meeting residency.
[03:41] Ravi Patel: Absolutely — our routing policy can direct requests by region, user, or latency. Hybrid setups are common: pin EU traffic to Private, keep US on Dedicated, and use Hosted in APAC initially while we stand up Dedicated there. The platform supports fallbacks and canary rollouts too.
[03:55] Ben Carter: That helps. For the pilot, can we get a perf run that simulates our production payload — 1.2k tokens average, peak QPS 45 for summarization jobs and long-tail p95 latency target under 500ms?
[04:10] Ravi Patel: Yes, we'll design the benchmark. A few clarifications — is 1.2k tokens per request average with 5k max? And p95 target 500ms end-to-end or just inference?
[04:21] Alicia Gomez: That's average; max is around 5k tokens. And the 500ms is ideal for inference latency. If we need to be realistic we can target 700ms for complex prompts.
[04:33] Ravi Patel: Noted. For 5k tokens, quantized models may not hit your latency needs — we might recommend mixed strategy: full-precision for long-run critical flows, quantized for short ones. Also batch sizing will matter; we'll share batching config suggestions.
[04:48] Maya Chen: Quick pause — Sofia, what are the must-have compliance docs for you to sign off?
[04:53] Sofia Li: SOC2 Type II report, encryption architecture diagram, KMS/HSM attestation, and an audit of RBAC controls and admin audit logs. Possibly penetration test summary.
[05:05] Lena Ortiz: We'll assemble our SOC2 binder and a short security whitepaper. For HSM, we can share our KMS integration options and the supported HSM vendors.
[05:14] Tom Reed: Any SLA changes if we move to a multi-region dedicated setup? We need 99.9 for critical endpoints.
[05:21] Maya Chen: We can discuss SLA in the addendum — Dedicated SLA can be tightened with multi-AZ redundancy and active-active routing. We'll price the SLA delta.
[05:30] Ben Carter: Network question — what's the expected lead time to provision Dedicated capacity in APAC?
[05:36] Ravi Patel: Typically 3-6 weeks depending on instance availability and your sizing. If you need faster, we can spin up a Hosted-backed pool as interim.
[05:45] Alicia Gomez: That's acceptable. Timeline-wise we want the extension signed by end of Jan and pilot kickoff first week of Feb.
[05:53] Maya Chen: Okay so concrete timeline: contract addendum by Jan 26, Wyvern review Jan 27-29, sign Jan 31, pilot kickoff Feb 2. Does that match your internal schedule?
[06:04] Alicia Gomez: Yes that works.
[06:06] Sofia Li: One more point on data residency — for EU we need data at rest physically in EU for certain customers. Does Redwood Dedicated guarantee that?
[06:15] Ravi Patel: With Dedicated and Private you can pin storage and compute to EU regions so data at rest stays in-region; we'll document the storage topology and bring an architecture diagram.
[06:26] Tom Reed: Good. Any concerns about costs? If we commit more capacity, what's the discount ladder look like?
[06:33] Maya Chen: We have tiered reserved discounts — 10% at 1.5x baseline, 18% at 2.5x, and custom pricing for larger commits. We'll include the specific numbers in the addendum.
[06:44] Ben Carter: Understood. On RBAC — we need fine-grained role separation between ML engineers and data engineers and audit trails for all admin actions. Is that in Console today?
[06:54] Lena Ortiz: Yes Console supports RBAC roles and admin audit logs; for Dedicated we can ship logs to your SIEM.
[07:02] Alicia Gomez: Are there any pitfalls you typically see in these expansions?
[07:06] Ravi Patel: A couple — underestimating peak token mix (long prompts cost more), network misconfig (CIDR overlap causing peering issues), and forgetting to scope rollback policies (canary/fallback). We include a rollout checklist to mitigate.
[07:19] Tom Reed: That checklist will be helpful.
[07:21] Maya Chen: Alright wrapping up — recap: Redwood will send addendum + region pricing, perf benchmark plan, private deployment/KMS notes, and network checklist. Wyvern will confirm compliance list and VPC details. Pilot kickoff Feb 2.
[07:36] Alicia Gomez: Sounds good.
[07:38] Ben Carter: Thanks all.
[07:40] Sofia Li: Thanks.
[07:42] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and I'll drop the quote.

End of transcript.
